title: Reachability under composed runs
statement: Let $N$ and $M$ be nondeterministic Turing machines with Boolean symbols and respectively $K$ and $K'$ work tapes, on a fixed Boolean input $x$, and let $\phi$ map configurations of $N$ to configurations of $M$. Suppose that whenever a configuration $c$ of $N$ is not halted, one step of $M$ from $\phi(c)$ under any choice bit equals $\phi$ applied to the corresponding step of $N$. Let $P$ be a predicate on configurations of $M$. If $P$ holds at $\phi(N\text{'s run from }c\text{ under }u)$ for every choice word $u$, and if after any such run that halts, $P$ continues to hold after every further choice word of $M$ from its mapped configuration, then $P$ holds at the configuration reached by running $M$ on any choice word $w$ from $\phi(c)$.
hypotheses_covered: $K,K'\in\mathbb{N}$; $N,M$ are Boolean-symbol nondeterministic Turing machines with those work-tape counts
